Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-2784", "title": "Sleep Apnea", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Sleep apnea is a common disorder that causes your breathing to stop or get very shallow."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Breathing pauses can last from a few seconds to minutes."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "They may occur 30 times or more an hour."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The most common type is obstructive sleep apnea."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It causes your airway to collapse or become blocked during sleep."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Normal breathing starts again with a snort or choking sound."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "People with sleep apnea often snore loudly."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "However, not everyone who snores has sleep apnea."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "You are more at risk for sleep apnea if you are overweight, male, or have a family history or small airways."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Children with enlarged tonsils or adenoids may also get it."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Doctors diagnose sleep apnea based on medical and family histories, a physical exam, and sleep study results."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "When your sleep is interrupted throughout the night, you can be drowsy during the day."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "People with sleep apnea are at higher risk for car crashes, work-related accidents, and other medical problems."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "If you have it, it is important to get treatment."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Lifestyle changes, mouthpieces, surgery, and breathing devices can treat sleep apnea in many people."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-6", "title": "Prenatal Care", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Prenatal care is the health care you get while you are pregnant ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It includes your checkups and prenatal testing ."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Typically, a health care provider specializing in the delivery of babies and the care of pregnant women, such as an obstetrician or a midwife, provides prenatal care."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Prenatal care can help keep you and your fetus healthy until you're ready to deliver your baby ."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It lets your provider spot health problems early."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Early treatment can cure many problems and prevent others from developing."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Every prenatal visit offers you the chance to ask questions about having a healthy pregnancy and preparing for delivery."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Talk to your provider about childbirth education classes for you and your partner to help you prepare for the birth of your baby."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Your provider will give you a schedule for your prenatal visits."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Usually, visits during your pregnancy occur: Once a month for weeks 4 through 28 Twice a month for weeks 28 through 36 Weekly for week 36 until your baby is born If you are over 35 years old or your pregnancy is high risk because of health problems like diabetes or high blood pressure , your provider will probably want to see you more often."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "You can also expect to see your provider more often as your due date gets closer."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "During prenatal visits, your provider will check your health and carefully monitor your pregnancy until you deliver your baby."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Your first prenatal visit may take a little longer."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Your provider will most likely: Ask about your health history, including prior pregnancies Ask about your family's health history Discuss any health conditions and risk factors that could affect you or your fetus Do a complete physical exam, including a pelvic exam and Pap test Review blood, urine, or other routine prenatal lab tests Check your blood pressure, height, and weight Discuss a healthy amount of weight gain, healthy eating , and prenatal vitamins Figure out your due date (when you are 40 weeks pregnant) During most visits, your provider will most likely: Check your blood pressure and weight gain Measure your abdomen (belly) to check fetal growth once you begin to show Check the fetal heart rate Check your hands and feet for swelling Do routine prenatal tests Depending on the stage of your pregnancy, you may have additional tests."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Always talk to your provider before you start or stop any medicine ."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "To help keep yourself and your fetus healthy, avoid substances that could be harmful, such as tobacco, alcohol, and drugs."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "of Health and Human Services Office on Women's Health"}]}, {"id": "MLP-5624", "title": "Chronic Myeloid Leukemia", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Leukemia is a term for cancers of the blood cells."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Leukemia starts in blood-forming tissues such as the bone marrow."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your bone marrow makes the cells which will develop into white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Each type of cell has a different job: White blood cells help your body fight infection Red blood cells deliver oxygen from your lungs to your tissues and organs Platelets help form clots to stop bleeding When you have leukemia, your bone marrow makes large numbers of abnormal cells."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "This problem most often happens with white blood cells."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "These abnormal cells build up in your bone marrow and blood."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "They crowd out the healthy blood cells and make it hard for your cells and blood to do their work."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is a type of chronic leukemia."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "\"Chronic\" means that the leukemia usually gets worse slowly."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "In CML, the bone marrow makes abnormal granulocytes (a type of white blood cell)."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "These abnormal cells are also called blasts."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "When the abnormal cells crowd out the healthy cells, it can lead to infection, anemia , and easy bleeding ."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The abnormal cells can also spread outside the blood to other parts of the body."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "CML usually occurs in adults during or after middle age."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "What causes chronic myeloid leukemia (CML)?"}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Most people with CML have a genetic change called the Philadelphia chromosome."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "It's called that because researchers in Philadelphia discovered it."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "People normally have 23 pairs of chromosomes in each cell."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "These chromosomes contain your DNA (genetic material)."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "In CML, part of the DNA from one chromosome moves to another chromosome."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "It combines with some DNA there, which creates a new gene called BCR-ABL."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "This gene causes your bone marrow to make an abnormal protein."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "This protein allows the leukemia cells to grow out of control."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "The Philadelphia chromosome isn't passed from parent to child."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Who is at risk for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML)?"}, {"id": "S025", "text": "There are a few factors that could raise your risk: Age - your risk goes up as you get older CML is slightly more common in men Exposure to high-dose radiation What are the symptoms of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML)?"}, {"id": "S026", "text": "If you do have symptoms, they can include: Feeling very tired Weight loss for no known reason Drenching night sweats Fever Pain or a feeling of fullness below the ribs on the left side How is chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Your health care provider may use many tools to diagnose CML: A physical exam A medical history Blood tests, such as a complete blood count (CBC) with differential and blood chemistry tests."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Blood chemistry tests measure different substances in the blood, including electrolytes, fats, proteins, glucose (sugar), and enzymes."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Specific blood chemistry tests include a basic metabolic panel (BMP) , a comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) , kidney function tests , liver function tests , and an electrolyte panel ."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "There are two main types - bone marrow aspiration and bone marrow biopsy."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Both tests involve removing a sample of bone marrow and bone."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "The samples are sent to a lab for testing."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Genetic tests to look for gene and chromosome changes, including tests to look for the Philadelphia chromosome If you are diagnosed with CML, you may have additional tests such as imaging tests to see whether the cancer has spread."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "What are the phases of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML)?"}, {"id": "S035", "text": "The phases are based on how much the CML has grown or spread: Chronic phase, where less than 10% of cells in the blood and bone marrow are blast cells (leukemia cells)."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Most people are diagnosed in this phase, and many do not have symptoms."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Standard treatment usually helps in this phase."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Accelerated phase, 10% to 19% of the cells in the blood and bone marrow are blast cells."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "In this phase, people often have symptoms and standard treatment may not be as effective as in the chronic phase."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Blastic phase, where 20% or more of the cells in the blood or bone marrow are blast cells."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "The blast cells have spread to other tissues and organs."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "If you have tiredness, fever, and an enlarged spleen during the blastic phase, it is called a blast crisis."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "What are the treatments for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML)?"}, {"id": "S044", "text": "There are several different treatments for CML: Targeted therapy, which uses drugs or other substances that attack specific cancer cells with less harm to normal cells."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "For CML, the drugs are tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs)."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "They block tyrosine kinase, which is an enzyme that causes your bone marrow to make too many blasts."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "Chemotherapy Immunotherapy High-dose chemotherapy with stem cell transplant Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI)."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "DLI is a treatment that may be used after a stem cell transplant."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "It involves giving you an infusion (into your bloodstream) of healthy lymphocytes from the stem cell transplant donor."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Lymphocytes are a type of white blood cell."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "These donor lymphocytes may kill the remaining cancer cells."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "Surgery to remove the spleen (splenectomy) Which treatments you get will depend on which phase you are in, your age, your overall health, and other factors."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "When the signs and symptoms of CML are reduced or have disappeared, it is called remission."}, {"id": "S054", "text": "The CML may come back after remission, and you may need more treatment."}]}, {"id": "MLP-7207", "title": "Acute Flaccid Myelitis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) is a neurologic disease ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It affects an area of the spinal cord called gray matter."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "This can cause the muscles and reflexes in the body to become weak."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Because of these symptoms, some people call AFM a \"polio-like\" illness."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "What causes acute flaccid myelitis (AFM)?"}, {"id": "S005", "text": "AFM can be caused by several different viruses."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Researchers think that enteroviruses have been causing the recent increases in the number of children with AFM."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "AFM can also be caused by other viruses, including flaviviruses, herpesviruses, and adenoviruses."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Most people with AFM had a mild respiratory illness or fever (like you would get from a viral infection ) before they got AFM."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Who is more likely to develop acute flaccid myelitis (AFM)?"}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Anyone can get AFM, but most cases (more than 90%) have been in young children."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "What are the symptoms of acute flaccid myelitis (AFM)?"}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Most people with AFM will suddenly have: Arm or leg weakness A loss of muscle tone and reflexes Some people also have other symptoms, including: Facial drooping/weakness Trouble moving the eyes Drooping eyelids Trouble swallowing Slurred speech Pain in the arms, legs, back, or neck Sometimes AFM can weaken the muscles that you need for breathing."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "This can lead to respiratory failure , which is very serious."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "If you get respiratory failure, you may need to use a ventilator (breathing machine) to help you breathe."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "If you or your child develops any of these symptoms, get medical care right away."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "How is acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S017", "text": "AFM causes many of the same symptoms as other neurologic diseases, such as transverse myelitis and Guillain-Barre syndrome ."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "To find out if you have AFM, your doctor may use: A neurologic exam , including looking at where there is weakness, poor muscle tone, and decreased reflexes An MRI to look at the spinal cord and brain Lab tests on the cerebrospinal fluid (the fluid around the brain and spinal cord) Nerve conduction and electromyography (EMG) studies ."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "These tests check nerve speed and the response of muscles to the messages from the nerves."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "It is important that the tests are done as soon as possible after the symptoms start."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "What are the treatments for acute flaccid myelitis (AFM)?"}, {"id": "S022", "text": "A doctor who specializes in treating brain and spinal cord illnesses (neurologist) may recommend treatments for specific symptoms."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "For example, physical and/or occupational therapy may help with arm or leg weakness."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Researchers do not know the long-term outcomes of people who get AFM."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Can acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) be prevented?"}, {"id": "S026", "text": "There is no specific way to prevent AFM."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "But you can take steps to prevent getting sick from a virus by: Washing your hands often with soap and water Avoiding touching your face with unwashed hands Avoiding close contact with people who are sick Cleaning and disinfecting surfaces that you frequently touch, including toys Covering coughs and sneezes with a tissue or upper shirt sleeve, not hands Staying home when sick Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-6545", "title": "Mosquito Bites", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Mosquitoes are insects that live all over the world."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "There are thousands of different species of mosquitoes; about 200 of those live in the United States."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Female mosquitoes bite animals and humans and drink a very small amount of their blood."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "They need protein and iron from blood to produce eggs."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "After drinking blood, they find some standing water and lay their eggs in it."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "The eggs hatch into larvae, then pupae, and then they become adult mosquitos."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The males live for about a week to ten days, and the females can live up to several weeks."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Some female mosquitoes can hibernate in the winter, and they can live for months."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "What health problems can mosquito bites cause?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Most mosquito bites are harmless, but there are times when they can be dangerous."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The ways that mosquito bites can affect humans include: Causing itchy bumps , as an immune system response to the mosquito's saliva."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "The bumps usually go away after a day or two."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Causing allergic reactions , including blisters, large hives, and in rare cases, anaphylaxis ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Anaphylaxis is a severe allergic reaction that affects the whole body."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Many of them do not have any treatments, and only a few have vaccines to prevent them."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "These diseases are more of a problem in Africa and other tropical areas of the world, but more of them are spreading to the United States."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "One factor is climate change , which makes the conditions in some parts of the United States more favorable to certain types of mosquitoes."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Other reasons include increased trade with, and travel to, tropical and subtropical areas."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Common diseases spread by mosquitoes include: Chikungunya , a viral infection that causes symptoms such as fever and severe joint pain."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "The symptoms usually last about a week, but for some, the joint pain may last for months."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Most cases of chikungunya in the United States are in people who traveled to other countries."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "There have been a few cases where it has spread in the United States."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Dengue , a viral infection that causes a high fever, headaches, joint and muscle pain, vomiting, and a rash."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Most people get better within a few weeks."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "In some cases, it can become very severe, even life-threatening."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Malaria , a parasitic disease that causes serious symptoms such as high fevers, shaking chills, and flu-like illness."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "It can be life-threatening, but there are drugs to treat it."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Malaria is a major health problem in many tropical and subtropical areas of the world."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Almost all cases of malaria in the United States are in people who traveled to other countries."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "West Nile Virus (WNV), a viral infection that often has no symptoms."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "In those that do have symptoms, they are usually mild, and include fever, headache, and nausea."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "In rare cases, the virus can enter the brain, and it can be life-threatening."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "WNV has spread across the continental United States."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Zika Virus , a viral infection that often does not cause symptoms."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "One in five infected people do get symptoms, which are usually mild."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "They include a fever, rash, joint pain, and pink eye."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Besides being spread by mosquitoes, Zika can spread from mother to baby during pregnancy and cause serious birth defects."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "It can also spread from one partner to another during sex."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "There have been a few outbreaks of Zika in the southern United States."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Use an insect repellent when you go outdoors."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Choose an Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)-registered insect repellent."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "They are evaluated to make sure they are safe and effective."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Make sure that the repellant has one of these ingredients: DEET, picaridin, IR3535, oil of lemon eucalyptus, or para-menthane-diol."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "It is important to follow the instructions on the label."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Wear long sleeves, long pants, and socks when outdoors."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Mosquitoes may bite through thin fabric, so spray thin clothes with an EPA-registered repellent like permethrin."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "Don't apply permethrin directly to skin."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "Install or repair screens on windows and doors to keep mosquitoes out."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Regularly empty standing water from your house and yard."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "The water could be in flowerpots, gutters, buckets, pool covers, pet water dishes, discarded tires, or birdbaths."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "If you plan to travel, get information about the areas you will be going to."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "Find out whether there is a risk of diseases from mosquitoes, and if so, whether there is a vaccine or medicine to prevent those diseases."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "See a health care provider familiar with travel medicine, ideally 4 to 6 weeks before your trip."}]}]
